Subject: Retail PoC — recommended engine slate, latency/cost tradeoffs and next steps

Hi Sam / Lena —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a recommended path for the PoC based on the prompts and call notes:

What we heard
- 95th pct latency target: ~300ms for single-turn product search and suggestion flows.
- Throughput: bursts up to ~120 reqs/min with sustained ~25 reqs/min overnight.
- Budget sensitivity: want to keep hosted inference unit cost low while avoiding >2x regret on quality.
- Security: logs must be retained for 90 days; SOC2 evidence requested during procurement.

Recommended candidate slate (shortlist and rationale)
1) small-llama-quant-8b (managed variant) — Best cost-to-quality for retrieval-augmented responses; median latency ~180ms on our hosted nodes, token cost low. Good for scaled product suggestion use-cases where hallucination risk is modest.
2) redwood-rl-13b-fp16 — Better on instruction-following and multi-step rewrite flows; median latency ~320ms, higher cost but noticeably fewer regressions on shopping-cart prompts.
3) redwood-7b-opt (low-latency dedicated) — If you decide to go Dedicated, this variant gives sub-200ms median with reserved capacity guarantees and predictable unit economics.

Benchmarks and artifacts
- Attached: veraretail_benchmarks_q2.csv (sample prompts from your session), prompt-set-retail-v1.jsonl (prompt pack we used), cost-latency-estimates.pdf (rolled-up comparisons).
- Live dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.com/benchmarks/veraretail-q2

Key tradeoffs (short)
- Cost vs latency: small-llama-quant-8b gives lowest cost but can underperform on long-context disambiguation.
- Quality regressions: we saw 2.1% drop in QA pass rate on a corner prompt set vs redwood-rl-13b; those samples are flagged in the attached CSV.
- Operational: Dedicated offers the tightest SLA for p95, but requires commit (we provided a 3-month pilot commit estimate in cost-latency-estimates.pdf).

Proposed next steps
1) Your ask: choose 1 hosted candidate + 1 Dedicated candidate we should instrument for a 2-week pilot.
2) Redwood: provide a short Pilot MEP (metrics, evaluation prompts, rollback criteria) and a cleaned prompt pack tailored to your product flows.
3) Procurement: we’ll attach SOC2 artifacts and a sample SOW for the pilot.

If helpful I can hop on a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to walk the spreadsheet and answer budget questions.

Thanks —
Irene

--
Irene Choi | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — quick answers below and a couple of operational notes.

1) Hosted cost (approximate, USD per 1k queries, aggregated):
- small-llama-quant-8b: $6–$8 per 1k (typical retail prompts, token length ~120).
- redwood-rl-13b-fp16: $15–$20 per 1k.
Notes: redwood-rl-13b runs ~2.5x the token cost vs small-llama-quant-8b in our tests; actual invoice depends on tokenization and response length.

2) Dedicated reservation to achieve sub-200ms p95:
- For the traffic shape you described (bursts to 120 reqs/min), a 2-GPU pool (A100 class) with continuous batching configured should meet the p95 target for redwood-7b-opt and small-llama-quant-8b. We included a 2-week pilot commit option in the attached PDF.

3) On the flagged regressions:
- ~70% are long-context disambiguation cases (multi-sku context + typed queries). ~20% are typos/noisy input. ~10% are core-catalog canonical lookups — those are the highest priority to address with prompt engineering / retrieval tuning.

Operational asks:
- If Vera wants to prioritize cost, start pilot with small-llama-quant-8b hosted and measure QA pass rate on the 1000-sample validation set we provided.
- If you want lower regression risk on rewrite/checkout flows, add redwood-rl-13b as an instrumented secondary model and failover target.

I’ll prepare a one-page cost/latency appendix and our SOC2 artifact bundle for procurement.

—Karthik
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
